text: We provide enterprise cloud infrastructure and managed compute. Recurring subscription revenue grew as customers migrated workloads to our platform and expanded seat-based licensing across business units.
Our data warehouse and analytics service is sold on a consumption model. Net revenue retention improved on higher query volume and broader adoption of our developer tooling and API products.

Annual recurring revenue increased on strength in our developer collaboration suite. Gross margins expanded as more workloads moved to multi-tenant SaaS deployments and enterprise renewals accelerated.
Net interest income rose with higher loan balances and improved deposit pricing. Credit quality remained stable while our allowance for loan losses reflected a cautious macroeconomic outlook.
Our consumer and commercial lending portfolios expanded. Tier 1 capital ratios stayed strong and fee income from wealth management partially offset margin compression in the deposit franchise.
Mortgage origination volume declined while net charge-offs stayed low. We grew core deposits and maintained liquidity coverage well above regulatory minimums during the period.
Upstream production volumes increased across our shale acreage. Realized prices for crude and natural gas drove cash flow, and we reduced drilling costs per well through operational efficiency.
Our renewable generation portfolio expanded with new solar and wind capacity. Power purchase agreements provide contracted cash flows, and transmission investments support grid interconnection.
Exploration and production segment benefited from higher commodity prices. We hedged a portion of expected output and prioritized capital discipline while returning cash to shareholders.
Comparable store sales declined on softer discretionary demand. We managed inventory tightly, expanded our e-commerce channel, and protected gross margin through promotional discipline.
Foot traffic weakened across mall-based locations. Omnichannel fulfillment and loyalty program growth supported revenue, while freight and shrink pressured operating margins.
Grocery same-store sales grew on unit volume and private-label penetration. We invested in distribution centers and digital ordering to offset wage inflation and competitive pricing.
